A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E support comparison, including readable equations, tables and figures. Existing content can be matched despite reformatting and appendix additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on CIFAR-10, FFHQ and MNIST, including generalization scores, entropy, FID, generated samples and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional FFHQ and accumulation results in Appendix D.1–D.2.

M1.justification: The entropy-based selection objective, Greedy Selection, Threshold Decay Filter, DINOv2 feature distances and diffusion architectures are retained. Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 specify the same procedures.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, FFHQ, MNIST, replace and accumulation settings, classifier-free guidance, and the fresh-real-data scenario already appear in v1. The added appendix analyses investigate retained coverage; larger FFHQ subsets change sample sizes, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the vanilla paradigms, unconditional/CFG alternatives, unfiltered 2N-sample control and random-sampling baseline. The new appendix diagnostics introduce no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds FFHQ sample-size settings of 16,384 and 32,768 alongside 8,192 for the entropy–generalization analysis. Existing experiments retain their reported architectures, training budgets, sampling settings and metrics.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.1–D.2 adds an FFHQ accumulation memorization case study and checks whether the entropy–generalization relationship holds across datasets and paradigms. Existing sample-count, filter-ratio, decay-rate and distribution-spikiness analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The Pearson correlation of 0.91 and near-zero p-value are retained. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed information or uncertainty intervals; the additional scatter observations introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Figure 12 shows FFHQ generated/nearest-training pairs becoming more similar across accumulation iterations. Figure 13 adds FFHQ and accumulation observations supporting the existing entropy–generalization trend. Earlier figure results and both tables are unchanged, including Table 2 FIDs of 28.0, 30.8 and 27.5.

T1.justification: The differential-entropy definition, generalization score, KL estimator, selection objective, MNND definition and entropy–MNND inequality are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a generalization-to-memorization transition, its relationship to declining entropy, and mitigation through entropy-based selection. Additional appendix support does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1 newly clarifies that fewer than ten accumulation iterations cannot establish whether generalization scores approach zero or a positive lower bound. D.2 interprets the expanded scatter results as suggesting a dataset-independent entropy indicator. Existing theoretical and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds paper-specific project-page and code links on its opening page. Appendix B retains the same architecture, optimizer, epoch, feature-extractor, hardware and pseudocode information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior collapse, memorization and data-selection research are retained. Abbreviated citation labels and expanded bibliographic author names are formatting changes.

P1.justification: The three findings become numbered Sections 3.1–3.3, with expanded contents entries and brief pointers to the new appendix analyses. Local wording, acknowledgements and header information change, while most existing prose and the narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns the presentation with a shaded title/abstract panel, colored sans-serif headings, a standalone contents page and revised figure placement. Figure 1 moves to the opening page, and new Figures 12–13 are added. All earlier figure artwork and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix D.1–D.2 provides useful additional support beyond the original CIFAR-focused correlation analysis and explicitly limits conclusions about long-term convergence. New code/project pointers and clearer navigation improve usability. These are limited gains: the main results remain unchanged, and the acknowledged lack of a rigorous explanation of entropy collapse is unresolved.
